name: DS18B20
description: Digital temperature sensor that communicates over a single-wire 1-Wire bus, needing only one data line (plus ground) to a microcontroller. Each device has a unique 64-bit factory-lasered ROM code, so many sensors can share one bus. It reports temperature in 9 to 12 bits of user-configurable resolution and operates from 3.0 to 5.5 V. It can also draw power parasitically from the data line, removing the need for a dedicated VDD connection.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: optional 3.0-5.5 V supply; tie to GND for parasite-power mode

typical_application: Multi-drop temperature monitoring (thermostats, HVAC, equipment thermal monitoring) where multiple sensors share a single MCU GPIO over a long bus.
gotchas: DQ requires an external pull-up resistor, typically 4.7k to VDD, for normal operation
TO-92 pin order (flat face toward you, leads down) is GND, DQ, VDD left-to-right; reversing VDD and GND can destroy the part
in parasite-power mode VDD is tied to GND and a strong bus pull-up (e.g. MOSFET) is needed during temperature conversion
12-bit conversions take up to 750 ms; do not poll faster than the conversion completes
counterfeit DS18B20 parts are common and often have poor accuracy or wrong ROM behavior
long bus runs need proper pull-up sizing and may require lower resolution or an active pull-up for reliability
